rows.text: Niv-Mizzet draws you a card whenever ANY player casts an instant or sorcery, and pings for one whenever you draw. In a four-player pod that means the rest of the table is running your engine for you, and every counterspell you hold up is a cantrip that also deals damage. The deck is built to sit behind open mana, answer whatever matters, and convert the table's own spells into a clock.

rows.name: Niv-Mizzet, Parun
rows.text: six mana, three blue and three red, uncounterable, and a 5/5 flier. Every instant or sorcery cast by anybody draws you a card; every card you draw deals one damage anywhere.

rows.name: Harmonic Prodigy
rows.text: Niv-Mizzet is a Dragon WIZARD, so both of his triggers double. Every instant or sorcery anyone casts draws you two, and each of those draws pings twice. Two mana for four times the output.

rows.name: Ghyrson Starn, Kelermorph
rows.text: whenever another source you control deals EXACTLY one damage, Ghyrson deals two more. Niv's ping is exactly one, so every draw becomes three damage. With Harmonic Prodigy also out, a single opposing cantrip deals twelve.

rows.name: Basilisk Collar
rows.text: deathtouch and lifelink on Niv. Now every one-damage ping kills a creature and gains you life. It turns the engine into a board wipe.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: haste and shroud, because a six-mana commander that eats a removal spell is a lost game.

rows.name: Slip Out the Back
rows.text: one mana to phase him out of removal, and it leaves a counter behind.

guide.title: Everything you hold up is also a draw

rows.name: Counterspell
rows.text: the clean two-mana answer, and it draws you a card off your own cast.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: counter, and the mana casts Niv next turn.

rows.name: Mana Sculpt
rows.text: the same idea with a Wizard on the battlefield, which you almost always have.

rows.name: Force of Negation
rows.text: free on their turn.

rows.name: Fierce Guardianship
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Pact of Negation
rows.text: free now; the upkeep payment is easy in a deck holding this much mana.

rows.name: Flusterstorm
rows.text: nearly unbeatable in a counter war, and each copy is another Niv trigger.

rows.name: Dispel
rows.text: one mana that answers the removal spell aimed at Niv.

rows.name: An Offer You Can't Refuse
rows.text: one mana for any noncreature spell.

rows.name: Mystical Dispute
rows.text: one mana against blue decks.

rows.name: Pyroblast
rows.text: one mana to counter or destroy anything blue. The colour hosers are maindeck here on purpose — a four-player pod nearly always has a blue or red deck in it.

rows.name: Red Elemental Blast
rows.text: the second copy.

rows.name: Hydroblast
rows.text: the mirror, against red decks.

rows.name: Blue Elemental Blast
rows.text: and its partner.

rows.name: Aether Gust
rows.text: sends a red or green spell or permanent to the top or bottom of their library.

rows.name: Guttersnipe
rows.text: two damage to each opponent for every instant or sorcery YOU cast. On a turn where you counter two things that is twelve damage across the table.

rows.name: Gandalf, Goblins' Bane
rows.text: one damage to each opponent per noncreature spell — and one damage is exactly what Ghyrson Starn wants, so it becomes three to each opponent instead.

rows.name: Archmage Emeritus
rows.text: a card for every instant or sorcery you cast or copy, which is another Niv ping on top of the Niv draw.

rows.name: Lightning Bolt
rows.text: three damage for one mana, or a removal spell.

rows.name: Mizzium Mortars
rows.text: kills a creature, or overloaded, kills their whole board.

rows.name: Desolation of Smaug
rows.text: three damage to every non-Dragon creature — Niv survives — and it refunds four mana toward a Dragon.

rows.name: Rhystic Study
rows.text: in a deck already holding up mana, they rarely pay.

rows.name: Mystic Remora
rows.text: the best card in the deck on turns one through four.

rows.name: Brainstorm
rows.text: three draws with Niv out, so three pings.

rows.name: Impulse
rows.text: dig four, and it is an instant so it triggers Niv on your own turn.

rows.name: Frantic Search
rows.text: free, two draws, and it untaps three lands to keep interaction up.

rows.name: Fact or Fiction
rows.text: at instant speed, and every card drawn is a ping.

rows.name: Memory Deluge
rows.text: scales with your mana, and flashback makes it twice.

rows.name: Faithless Looting
rows.text: cheap filtering, twice.

rows.name: Big Score
rows.text: two cards and two Treasures at instant speed.

rows.name: Goblin Electromancer
rows.text: every instant and sorcery costs one less, which is how you double-spell on their turn.

rows.name: Arcane Signet
rows.text: the double-blue and double-red pips on Niv are the real cost of the deck.

rows.name: Izzet Signet
rows.text: fixes both halves.

rows.name: Chromatic Lantern
rows.text: makes every land produce whatever pip you are short.

rows.name: Coldsteel Heart
rows.text: cheap and colour-fixing.

rows.name: Fellwar Stone
rows.text: usually taps for exactly what you need in a multicolour pod.

rows.name: Firemind Vessel
rows.text: two different colours a turn.

rows.name: High Tide
rows.text: on a heavy-Island board this is a genuine explosive turn, and it costs one mana so it also triggers Niv.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift
rows.text: overloaded, it is the clear for a lethal Niv attack or the answer to a locked board.

rows.name: Echoing Truth
rows.text: bounces a permanent AND every copy of it — the answer to a token swarm.

rows.name: Aetherize
rows.text: returns every attacking creature to hand. In a pod that folds an entire alpha strike for four mana.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: the only answer to an enchantment in these colours.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free, and it redirects the removal spell aimed at Niv.

rows.name: Charisma
rows.text: on a deathtouch or pinging creature, it steals whatever it damages.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep fixing. Three blue and three red pips is a genuinely hard cost — Signets, Coldsteel Heart and Chromatic Lantern are what make Niv a turn-five or six play instead of a turn-eight one.
Play at instant speed. Every spell you cast on somebody else's turn is a Niv trigger you would have got anyway plus a card, and holding up two mana is almost always better than tapping out.

rows.name: Ghyrson Starn, Kelermorph
rows.text: three mana, and it triples every ping in the deck. Find it before you find another counterspell.

rows.name: Basilisk Collar
rows.text: the moment it is on Niv, the table's creatures stop mattering. Prioritise it against creature decks over any additional card draw.
